excerpt: Why drivers flee crashes in North Charleston, and what coverage pays when the driver is never found.
keyTakeaways: Hit-and-run accidents can leave North Charleston victims with no identified driver to claim against. Uninsured motorist (UM) coverage is the primary recovery path when the at-fault driver is unidentified. South Carolina requires uninsured motorist (UM) coverage on every auto policy (S.C. Code § 38-77-150); underinsured motorist (UIM) coverage must be offered but can be declined (S.C. Code § 38-77-160). Hit-and-run is a criminal offense under S.C. Code § 56-5-1210, and victims may also access the Crime Victims' Compensation Fund. The 3-year filing deadline (S.C. Code § 15-3-530) applies to civil claims.

faqs.question: Why do drivers flee the scene of a crash in North Charleston?
faqs.answer: Usually because stopping carries a separate consequence for them. Among drivers who fled fatal crashes and were later caught, two in five had no valid license (AAA Foundation for Traffic Safety, 2026); others are uninsured, impaired or wanted on a warrant. Driving under suspension is itself a crime in South Carolina (S.C. Code § 56-1-460).

faqs.question: How many South Carolina drivers are uninsured?
faqs.answer: Estimates vary by source and year. What matters for your claim is that drivers without insurance may flee to avoid financial liability, and South Carolina requires uninsured motorist coverage on every auto policy (S.C. Code § 38-77-150), which is often what pays when the driver is never identified.

faqs.question: Who is most often hurt in hit-and-run crashes?
faqs.answer: The most vulnerable road users. Pedestrians cannot get a plate number while lying injured, cyclists are frequently left in the roadway, and late-night victims have fewer witnesses and a harder time identifying the vehicle.

faqs.question: Can I recover compensation if the driver is never identified?
faqs.answer: Often yes, through your own uninsured motorist coverage, if you report the crash to police within a reasonable time; can show physical contact with the other vehicle, an independent witness who signs an affidavit or, since 2024, a recording of the crash; and were not negligent in failing to identify the driver (S.C. Code § 38-77-170). Identifying the driver through investigation and crime victims' compensation are the other routes worth exploring.

faqs.question: Will traffic cameras show who hit me in North Charleston?
faqs.answer: Probably not. SCDOT traffic cameras stream in real time and do not record, so there is no state footage to request. Look quickly for business security, home doorbell and other drivers' dash-camera footage, which is often overwritten within days. Since 2024, a recording of the crash can take the place of physical contact or a witness affidavit in an uninsured motorist claim when the driver is never identified (S.C. Code § 38-77-170).
